business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: The chart below sets forth our business model: For further details in relation to our corporate and fund structure, see “—Description of our Business—Fund Structure” on page 232. 220 We derive our income primarily from three income streams (i) Management Fee; (ii) Carried Interest; and (iii) Income from Sponsor Commitment. 221 Our business model does not require substantial investment in fixed assets; however, certain aspects of our operations are capital-intensive.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: There is no physical supply chain; the relevant integration is vertical integration of the fund-management value chain and full capture of fund economics into the listed entity. (1) Economic integration: 'All the income generated from the funds managed and advised by us, across the three income streams, is received in its entirety by us. Our objective has been to capture the economic value generated by the funds managed and advised by us within our Company, with the goal of enhancing our enterprise value and strengthening our balance sheet.' No Carried Interest is allocated to any individual — 'all the Carried Interest generated across our Gaja Capital Funds is attributable to our Company without any specific allocation to any individual'. (2) Structural integration: the Company acts as investment manager to the India-domiciled AIF constituents while its own subsidiary Gaja Advisors Ltd, Mauritius acts as investment manager to the Mauritius-domiciled constituent funds, and Eastgate Secondaries Advisor LLP (in which the Company holds an investment) will manage the proposed Secondaries Fund; operations run through seven subsidiaries (four Indian, one overseas, two overseas step-down). (3) Backward integration into distribution (fund-raising): 'We have traditionally relied on our network of investors to raise funds for the Gaja Capital Funds while keeping the proportion of funds raised through third-party distributors low' — three distributors used in Fiscal 2024 and none in Fiscal 2025 or Fiscal 2026. (4) Balance-sheet integration into the funds: sponsor commitments substantially above the SEBI AIF Regulations threshold (Rs 2,740.00 million, 6.41% of total fund size as of March 31, 2026, against a prescribed 2.5% of corpus or Rs 50.00 million, whichever is lower), the past warehousing of an investment in a portfolio company for Fund IV on the Company's own balance sheet, and investment of balance-sheet capital in third-party funds to bolster deal flow. (5) Forward integration into the Portfolio Companies via the four-professional Operating Team's 'invest-and-collaborate' model operating at three engagement levels (board participation; strategic areas; operational support), with board representation in nearly all Portfolio Companies. (6) Outsourced functions are explicitly limited: 'We work with professional firms for support across accounting, legal and valuation related matters'; fund administration is staffed by 7 contractual personnel. Headcount as of March 31, 2026: 37 total — 23 permanent (Core Team 15, comprising Investment Team 10, Operating Team 4, Investor Relations 1; Finance Team 3; IT 1; Administrative staff 3; Compliance Team 1) and 14 contractual (Fund Administration 7; Housekeeping and Security 7), plus an Operating Advisors Group of two former CXOs. Attrition of total employees: 3 / 1 / 3 (13.33% / 4.76% / 16.22%) in Fiscal 2026 / 2025 / 2024, with nil attrition among Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management in all three fiscals.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Verbatim, under the RHP's own heading 'Seasonality' in Management's Discussion and Analysis (page 365): 'Our business is not subject to seasonal variations.' The RHP does, however, separately describe the timing of Carried Interest as unpredictable rather than seasonal — Risk Factor 3: 'The timing and receipt of Carried Interest from the funds managed and advised by us are unpredictable and will contribute to the volatility of our cash flows.' Management Fee is charged quarterly on capital committed/invested at the beginning of each quarter, and Income from Sponsor Commitment is recognised quarterly from fair valuation.
